title: Emmaus, slowly (Luke 24:13–35)
hookLine: stay with us, because it is towards evening

lines: ARE YOU THE ONLY ONE WHO DOESN'T KNOW?
cards: The same Sunday, in the afternoon. Two disciples are walking away from Jerusalem toward a village called Emmaus, about sixty furlongs off, seven miles or so. One is named Cleophas; the other Luke never names.
They're going over everything that has happened, the way people do after a funeral. A stranger falls into step and asks what they're discussing. They stop, faces sad.
Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem who doesn't know? Luke tells this slowly, and the slowness is the point.

teach.b: They tell him the whole story, and their grief is in the past tense: we hoped that it was he that should have redeemed Israel. We hoped.
The stranger walks them through the scriptures, beginning with Moses and all the prophets, showing what they said about the Christ. It takes miles.

At the village, he makes as if to keep going, and they won't let him: "But they constrained him; saying: Stay with us, because it is towards evening, and the day is now far spent. And he went in with them."
At table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it, and gives it to them. "And their eyes were opened, and they knew him: and he vanished out of their sight."

teach.h: THE SCRIPTURES OPENED ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Their hearts, they say, were burning while he opened the scriptures on the road, and that same hour they go back to Jerusalem to tell how he was known to them in the breaking of bread.
Catholic teaching sees the shape of the Mass here. First the word: the scriptures opened and explained. Then the table: bread taken, blessed, broken, given.

teach.h: STAY WITH US, IT IS TOWARDS EVENING.
teach.b: Saint John Paul the Second built his letter for the Year of the Eucharist around this scene and titled it with the disciples' plea in Latin, Mane nobiscum Domine, stay with us, Lord.

teach.h: KNOWN IN THE BREAKING OF BREAD.
teach.b: And notice: he doesn't force his way in. He would have walked on. The invitation is theirs.
Luke shows the risen Christ waiting to be asked.

how: Catholics hear the Emmaus story in Easter week and on the Third Sunday of Easter in one year of the cycle, and Catholic teaching points to it as the pattern of the Mass: the Liturgy of the Word, then the Liturgy of the Eucharist.

o: the village where two knew him at the table
the hill outside Jerusalem where he rose
the town where Jesus grew up as a boy

games.q: the road to Emmaus — tap the pairs.
p: their grief, in the past tense

s: Luke names both disciples on the road
he names Cleophas; the other is never named.
they recognized him while he explained the scriptures
their hearts burned on the road, but their eyes were opened at the breaking of bread.
John Paul II named a letter after their plea
Mane nobiscum Domine, stay with us, Lord, for the Year of the Eucharist.

games.q: you've walked seven miles with a stranger who made the scriptures burn. you reach your village at dusk, and he starts to walk on. what do you do?
o: beg him to stay with you.
ask his name before he goes.
games.why: they constrained him: stay with us, because it is towards evening. he went in, broke the bread, and they knew him.

practice: Think back over today as if it were a road: where were you walking, what were you talking about, what did you hope for that didn't happen? Let it be there, the way it was for those two, and picture the evening coming in.
If you pray, use their words, stay with us, because it is towards evening; if you don't, just notice what you'd want to stay with you tonight.

wordCard.voice: Emmaus. The village seven miles from Jerusalem where two disciples knew the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread. Nobody is certain where it was. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, from the Vulgate of Luke 24:29: stay with us. John Paul II's 2004 letter takes its title from it.

carryVoice: Your line: stay with us. A plea at dusk, and a guest who said yes. Day four hundred eighty-eight, done.

sources.q: But they constrained him; saying: Stay with us, because it is towards evening, and the day is now far spent. And he went in with them.
And their eyes were opened, and they knew him: and he vanished out of their sight.
